what_it_does: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are AI models that reason about relationships — for example, recommending products by treating users and items as nodes in a graph with edges representing past interactions. For real-time online services the model must process a new query node by gathering information from its neighbors, then neighbors of neighbors, and so on; the number of nodes to touch grows exponentially with each layer, causing memory access to explode. This paper proposes EOD, which pre-computes and stores compressed summaries of node neighborhoods during offline preparation so that online inference only needs to look up these summaries rather than traversing the graph live. The compression uses a technique that exploits large blocks of zero values — skipping over zeros rather than storing them — to keep the summaries compact. To handle the remaining heavy memory access efficiently, EOD includes a Near-Memory Processing unit — a small compute engine placed physically close to, or inside, the memory chips — so that the feature aggregation math happens right where the data lives, avoiding the slow data transfer between memory and the main processor.
